original_turns_through_checkpoint.text: Good morning. I have Marcus Reed checked in for the cardiology rhythm clinic, but I want to confirm I have the correct Marcus Reed before I open anything.
I am Marcus Reed, born July 18, 1979. I was told to come in because my atrial fibrillation has been staying fast and they are planning a cardioversion.
I am his sister Nina. I drove him in today and can help with the parking and arrival times if the schedule changes.
Marcus, do you want Nina to receive any information from this episode of care, or only logistical details such as check-in times and where to park?
Only logistics through Monday. She can hear arrival times, where I need to go, and basic transportation instructions, but not medication changes, lab results, adherence history, or chart notes.

Consent note entered: Nina Reed may receive scheduling and transportation logistics through Monday only. Clinical results, medication details, adherence history, and social-work notes remain restricted.
Thank you. What is your everyday phone number for routine registration?
My regular cell is 617-555-0104, but that is not the number I want used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or my heart rhythm.
Okay. What backup contact should we use if nursing or cardiology cannot reach your cell?

Use Cedar Bridge Recovery House front desk at 617-555-0140 for daytime only. Please ask them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and do not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing on any message.
Understood. Do you want that backup contact used only if your cell does not answer or also for routine reminders?
Only if my cell does not answer. Routine reminders should go to the portal whenever possible.

Contact preference note entered: primary cell 617-555-0104. Backup daytime contact is Cedar Bridge Recovery House front desk 617-555-0140 only if the cell does not answer. Generic callback wording only; do not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing.
Do you have a support person for the actual ride home after sedation, or is that still undecided?
Still undecided. Nina can help with this morning, but I may use a program driver or someone else on procedure day.
That is fine. I only need the times so I know whether to take off work.
I will keep it to logistics. Please have a seat and Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first.
Marcus, come with me. Nina, I can update you on arrival windows if Marcus keeps that logistics-only setting active.
Tell me what has been happening with your symptoms over the past week.
I have had fluttering in my chest most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday, but I did not pass out.
Any chest pain, black stools, vomiting blood, or sudden weakness?
No chest pain and no bleeding. Just the racing heartbeat and feeling washed out.
Let me review your medications exactly as you are taking them right now.
Apixaban 5 milligrams twice a day, metoprolol tartrate 25 milligrams twice a day, lisinopril 10 milligrams every morning, and omeprazole 20 milligrams daily.
Have you taken anything over the counter for pain or colds?
I took ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before I remembered I probably should not with the blood thinner.
That is important. We will likely tell you to stop ibuprofen because it raises bleeding risk with apixaban.
Have you missed any doses of apixaban in the last month?
I have not missed any morning doses. I might have been late by a few hours last Monday night when I was changing locations, but I still took that pill before bed.
I will document that as possible delayed but not skipped Monday-night dose. Any completely missed doses in the last three weeks?
None that I remember. I know they were strict about not missing it before cardioversion.
Good. What about alcohol, supplements, or stimulants that could affect rhythm?
No energy drinks. I am focusing on recovery and do not want those details discussed with family.
I hear you. I will keep family updates limited to the logistics scope you set.

Nursing intake summary: symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, no active bleeding, possible delayed Monday-night apixaban dose but no confirmed skipped dose, ibuprofen used last week and should be reviewed.
I am getting your vitals now. Heart rate is 128, blood pressure 132 over 86, oxygen 98 percent on room air.
I am placing orders for CBC, BMP, magnesium, TSH, and a repeat ECG before Dr. Patel comes in.
I have the tubes labeled. Marcus, I am drawing blood now and the results should be back before the cardiologist finalizes the plan.
Thanks. Please use the cell first for any result callbacks unless that fails.
Understood. I do not need the backup details unless cardiology requests them.
Your sister asked at the desk whether the timing changed. I told her only that you are still being evaluated and we have not set the final arrival time.
That is exactly what I want. She can know the times later, not the reason anything changes.

Hi Marcus, I reviewed the emergency-department tracing and today's ECG. You are still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, but you are stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan.
Is cardioversion still the plan, or are we trying to just slow the rate?
Cardioversion is still the plan. Based on what we know so far, we were aiming for Wednesday morning, but I want the lab results and the medication history fully reconciled first.
Until then, continue apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily without interruption. Increase metoprolol tartrate from 25 milligrams twice daily to 37.5 milligrams twice daily starting tonight.
Stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Use acetaminophen instead if needed, and start magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights because your previous magnesium trend has been low-normal.
Keep lisinopril 10 milligrams daily for now, but hold the morning dose on the day of the procedure once the date is finalized.
So right now I keep taking apixaban, I raise the metoprolol tonight, I stop ibuprofen, and I begin the magnesium tonight?
Correct. Also do not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion.

Cardiology plan update: continue apixaban 5 mg BID without interruption, increase metoprolol tartrate to 37.5 mg BID starting tonight, stop ibuprofen/NSAIDs, use acetaminophen if needed, start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights, continue lisinopril 10 mg daily but hold morning dose on procedure day.
Your labs are back: hemoglobin 14.1, potassium 4.1, magnesium 1.7, creatinine 1.0, and TSH 1.9.
Those labs are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, and the magnesium result supports the supplement plan we just discussed.
I just got a tentative slot. Direct cardioversion is being held for Wednesday, March 11 at 10:20 AM with 8:50 AM arrival in the cardiac procedures unit.

Prep for that slot would be nothing by mouth after midnight except small sips of water for approved morning medications. We will confirm whether that slot stays direct cardioversion or changes to a TEE-guided case.
Please put that in the chart, and Nina can hear only the Wednesday time and arrival window, nothing about the medication plan.
All I need is whether I should block off Wednesday morning.
At the moment, yes: Wednesday morning, 8:50 arrival for a 10:20 procedure. Any clinical questions need to go through Marcus.
Scheduling note: logistics-only family access still active through Monday. Current tentative slot is Wednesday March 11, 8:50 AM arrival for 10:20 AM procedure in cardiac procedures.
Marcus, this is Klein from cardiology pharmacy. I am calling to make sure the new metoprolol dose is clear.
Please go ahead.
You are moving to 37.5 milligrams twice daily. Since you have 25-milligram tablets, that means one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening.
And apixaban stays 5 milligrams twice daily, no holding it before the procedure unless the cardiologist specifically tells me?
Exactly. Do not stop or skip apixaban on your own. The only routine hold we discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed.
Also, magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while you are on apixaban.
Thanks. Please do not call the Cedar Bridge number unless my cell fails.
Documented. I only needed the medication plan and contact preference, not any other social details.
Marcus, anesthesia reviewed the schedule and Wednesday will not work. The earliest available slot moved to Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.
Can Nina be told the new arrival time but not why it changed?
Yes. That still falls inside the logistics-only scope you gave through Monday, and I will leave the reason out.
Schedule update: Wednesday slot released. New tentative procedure slot is Thursday March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.
One more thing, Marcus. The nurse note says your Monday-night apixaban dose may have been delayed. Tell me exactly how uncertain that is.
I am pretty sure I took it, but it was late and I cannot prove the time. I do not want anyone telling Nina that this came up.
Understood. Because the timing is uncertain, I am changing the plan from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so we can check for clot first and still avoid an unnecessary delay.
The Thursday slot remains useful, but it is now specifically a TEE-guided cardioversion case. Continue apixaban exactly as prescribed and do not miss any further doses.

Procedure-plan update: changed from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion because of uncertain timing of a recent apixaban dose. Family logistics access does not include disclosing this clinical reason.
I got a text saying the time moved. Is it because he forgot his blood thinner?
I can confirm the updated arrival time when Marcus permits, but I cannot discuss medication adherence or clinical reasons for the change.
Fine. What is the new arrival time then?
Right now it is Thursday, March 12, 9:40 AM arrival for an 11:10 AM procedure. That is the only detail I can share.
I have updated the arrival letter in the portal. Marcus, I also changed the prep line so it says TEE-guided cardioversion for your own portal copy.
That portal wording is fine for me, just not for family or voicemail messages.
I am calling only about the prior authorization. I see hospital outpatient sedation and cardiology procedure charges, but I do not need any family contact information beyond the standard cell.
That is fine. Please use the cell and portal; the backup line is only for failed reach attempts.
Marcus, cardiology asked me to help with transportation and confidential contact planning for procedure day.
That would help. I am staying at Cedar Bridge for now, and after five in the evening they stop routing calls through the front desk.
What is the evening number if the day desk is closed and the cell fails?
Use Cedar Bridge evening desk at 617-555-0162, but again only generic callback wording. Do not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing.
I will record that as a backup after-hours route only, with generic wording, and still keep your cell as the first contact.

Social-work logistics note: if cell 617-555-0104 fails after 5 PM, use Cedar Bridge Recovery House evening desk 617-555-0162 with generic callback wording only. Do not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing.
Also, I do not want Nina getting any more scheduling updates after today. She helped with intake, but I am taking over the logistics myself from here.
I can record that the prior logistics-only access ends now and that future appointment details should not be shared with Nina.
Consent change: family logistics access for Nina Reed is revoked as of Monday afternoon. Do not share future appointment details, procedure times, or callback instructions with Nina Reed.
Thanks for clarifying that. I will update the desk note so staff do not confirm future times to Nina.
Excuse me, I am Martha Reed checking in for a treadmill stress test. Someone at the desk almost handed me a cardiology arrival sheet that was not mine.
Thank you for catching that. We have two Reed patients this week and I am separating the files now.
Martha, I am Dr. Lee. Your stress-test paperwork is completely separate from Marcus Reed's chart.
Please make sure nobody mixes those charts up. I do not want another patient or another family member hearing my schedule or contact notes.
Absolutely. I added a same-surname caution note to the desk workflow and confirmed that your restricted contact note stays on your chart only.

I am Dr. Choi, the weekend covering clinician for urgent rate-control issues only if Dr. Patel is unavailable. I do not need your social-work details unless an urgent medication issue requires outreach.
That is fine. Weekend coverage for urgent rhythm questions is okay, but not broader sharing.

Coverage note: Dr. Choi has weekend urgent clinical coverage for Marcus Reed limited to rate/rhythm questions and immediate medication issues; this does not expand family access or nonclinical disclosure.
Another change came in from anesthesia. The Thursday room was taken by an add-on case, so your TEE-guided cardioversion moved to Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival.
Friday at eleven arrival, twelve-thirty procedure. Please send it only to me in the portal and not to Nina.
Done. Friday, March 13, 11:00 AM arrival, cardiac procedures unit, nothing by mouth after midnight except approved morning medications.
I am adding a desk-facing logistics note that family access is revoked and Friday timing should be given only to Marcus.
Final pre-procedure scheduling note: Friday March 13, 11:00 AM arrival for 12:30 PM TEE-guided cardioversion. Family logistics access remains revoked.
Marcus, I am reviewing tomorrow's prep. Nothing by mouth after midnight except small sips of water with approved morning medications.
Which medications do I actually take tomorrow morning? I do not want to mess this up.

Take apixaban 5 milligrams in the morning with a sip of water, take metoprolol tartrate 37.5 milligrams, and hold lisinopril until after the procedure. Magnesium can be taken tonight, not tomorrow morning.
And still no ibuprofen or naproxen, correct?
Correct. Avoid NSAIDs. Use acetaminophen if you need something for pain.

I am double-checking the active medication list before tomorrow: apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily, metoprolol tartrate 37.5 milligrams twice daily, lisinopril 10 milligrams daily but held tomorrow morning, omeprazole 20 milligrams daily, and magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for the five-night course.
That matches what I have written down.

This is Dr. Choi. Since I am on weekend backup after the procedure, I only need the clinical handoff: the Friday TEE-guided cardioversion time, the anticoagulation plan, and return precautions if symptoms recur.
I will send you the clinical handoff, but not the social-work housing contact since that is not needed for weekend coverage unless the patient cannot be reached through standard channels.
Prior authorization is cleared for Friday. Marcus, do you want the paper estimate mailed anywhere or portal only?
Portal only. Do not mail anything to any shared address right now.
I am confirming your Friday arrival again: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Only your chart has the restricted callback note.
